title: Bur: Growth, reproduction, mortality, distribution, and biomass of freshwater drum in Lake Erie
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
fishingMode: Research gill/trap nets and trawls, not angling
summary: Summer use of water less than 10 m deep and return to deeper water in late fall support a broad shallow-water seasonal mechanism.
limitations: Different lake and old food web; no transferable city magnitudes, exact dates or bite probabilities.

title: Carter et al.: Movement patterns of smallmouth and largemouth bass in and around a Lake Michigan harbor
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: Smallmouth moved between harbor and lake as conditions changed; largemouth movements were more confined to harbor.
limitations: Supports species-specific habitat use, not transfer of Illinois pier scores. Observed occupancy temperature is not an angling optimum.
locator: Original abstract in Illinois Natural History Survey author repository; JGLR 38:396–401; DOI 10.1016/j.jglr.2012.02.003

title: Michigan Sea Grant: Fish in Lake Michigan—Distribution of selected species
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
fishingMode: Distribution synthesis reviewed by fishery biologists
summary: Historical winter perch concentrations in southern Lake Michigan were generally deeper than summer nearshore concentrations; Green Bay differs.
limitations: Historical distribution map, not contemporary pier catches. Do not erase drowned-river-mouth migration or transfer Green Bay opportunity.
locator: PDF page 34, yellow perch text; MICHU-SG-81-600

title: Chorak et al.: Yellow perch genetic structure and habitat use among connected habitats in eastern Lake Michigan
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
geographicScope: Eastern Lake Michigan and connected drowned river mouths including Manistee and Pere Marquette
fishingMode: Genetic/habitat sampling; no pier catch-effort model
summary: Distinct stocks and seasonal habitat connections complicate a simple offshore-only winter assumption.
limitations: Autumn/winter movement inference does not locate fish at the covered pier. Connected-lake harvest is not pier evidence.
locator: Ecology and Evolution 9:8922–8932, especially discussion; DOI 10.1002/ece3.5219

title: Hanson et al.: Intersexual variation in seasonal behaviour and depth distribution of largemouth bass
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: Deepest habitat use in winter contrasts with littoral use during warm months.
limitations: Small inland lake; transfers a qualitative habitat mechanism only. Movement is not bite probability.

title: Reeve et al.: Winter behaviour and energetics of free-swimming largemouth bass
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: Continued slow winter swimming and probable feeding contradict complete winter inactivity.
limitations: Consumption inferred from models, not measured pier catchability; no automatic winter zero or numerical thermal response. File path contains 2024; journal publication is 2025.
locator: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 82:1–16; DOI 10.1139/cjfas-2024-0254

title: Kruckman: Diel and seasonal patterns of channel catfish movement and habitat use in the lower Wabash River
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: Seasonal bank habitat and nocturnal movement differ; activity did not follow a simple warmer-is-always-more-active rule.
limitations: Different river; cannot establish Grand Haven winter fish locations or convert activity to bite probability.
locator: Original thesis abstract, Eastern Illinois University, thesis 2504

title: Cooke and McKinley: Winter residency and activity patterns of channel catfish and common carp in a thermal discharge canal
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
geographicScope: Nanticoke generating station, Lake Erie; winter 1997–1998
fishingMode: Telemetry; some fish collected by winter angling
summary: Catfish remained mobile and used deeper portions of a thermal discharge canal.
limitations: Artificial heated canal; not a Grand Haven winter analogue. Retained as counterevidence to total inactivity, not as evidence of a covered winter fishery.
locator: Fisheries Management and Ecology 6:515–526; methods pp. 516–517; DOI 10.1046/j.1365-2400.1999.00175.x

title: Beam: Daily and seasonal movement, as related to habitat use, of smallmouth bass in the Huron River, Michigan
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: No significant seasonal difference in tracked ranges or displacements; results caution against a universal winter inactivity rule.
limitations: Inland river, not any covered pier. No direct support for winter pier scores.
locator: DNR Fisheries Research Report 1971; scanned abstract PDF page 10 and discussion pages 57–58 visually checked

title: Michigan DNR lake whitefish species account
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: Deep summer distribution and shallow early-winter spawning habitat support contrasting access seasons.
limitations: Spawning does not imply biting. General historical recovery wording is superseded by the 2025 agency decline notice for current magnitude.
access: Full page reviewed with web reader; direct download denied

title: Michigan DNR walleye species account
authority: Primary agency, original study or author institution; see title
summary: Winter feeding persists; spring spawning timing and fall deep-water techniques differ from summer methods.
limitations: Year-round species feeding does not establish a winter pier fishery; no transferred numeric catch rates.
access: Full page reviewed with web reader; direct download denied
